scenes.text: Reindeer eyes change color with the seasons, from gold in summer to deep blue in winter.
The part that changes is a mirror-like layer behind the retina, called the tapetum lucidum.
Most mammals have a golden one, and researchers say this seasonal change is unique.
In Arctic Norway, reindeer live through months of winter darkness and months of nonstop summer sun.
In the dark, their pupils stay wide open for months.
That blocks tiny vessels that drain fluid, so pressure builds inside the eye.
The pressure squeezes collagen fibers in the mirror layer closer together.
Spaced normally, the fibers reflect yellow light. Packed tightly, they reflect blue.
Researchers found winter eyes are at least a thousand times more sensitive to light.
Some scientists think other changes in the retina must help too.
The trade-off? Their winter vision is probably less sharp.
Reindeer can also see ultraviolet light, which we can't.
Lichen, their winter food, absorbs ultraviolet, so it shows up dark against bright snow.
Which eye color would you pick, gold or blue? Tell me below.

title: Reindeer eyes turn blue in winter 🦌
caption: A 2013 study found the mirror layer behind reindeer retinas shifts from gold in summer to blue in winter. Researchers say it makes their eyes far more sensitive to light during the long Arctic darkness.
